claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially has a homogeneous high-temperature BCC structure.
During cooling and subsequent thermal exposure, Al atoms locally order in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
During cooling and subsequent thermal exposure, Al atoms locally segregate in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Local Al ordering and segregation create lattice distortions.
The Al-associated lattice distortions act as heterogeneous nucleation sites for ordered BCC-derivative phases.
B2 or a similar intermetallic structure is a likely ordered derivative phase.
Local Al ordering and segregation reduce the energy barrier for heterogeneous nucleation.
The nucleation and growth of ordered regions cause the initially BCC matrix to develop multiple phases over time.
Slow cooling and intermediate-temperature holds provide more diffusion time for Al segregation and ordering than rapid quenching.
Rapid quenching freezes the high-temperature homogeneous BCC state with minimal Al diffusion and ordering.
Slow-cooled or thermally aged samples should contain more ordered-phase domain volume than rapidly quenched samples.
Slow-cooled or thermally aged samples should exhibit greater localized Al enrichment than rapidly quenched samples.
Ordered phases and localized Al segregation should produce detectable diffraction deviations and microscopy contrast.
The proposed mechanism should apply at intermediate temperatures and cooling rates that permit sufficient Al mobility and short-range ordering.
The proposed mechanism should not apply during sufficiently rapid quenching because Al mobility is inadequate.
Temperatures too high for ordering to persist should not produce the predicted multiphase behavior through this mechanism.
